title.title: Sharp one-third stability of Brenier maps
title.subtitle: Claim: optimal transport maps move at most like $W_2^{1/3}$, uniformly, and $1/3$ cannot be improved

plain: Move one pile of sand to another as cheaply as possible: nudge the target, and how far does the plan move?

beats.text: A Brenier map is the gradient of a convex potential; three pieces send mass to three atoms
Tilting the middle piece swaps a thin slab of source points between far-apart targets
That forces exponent $1/3$, not the conjectured $1/2$, and $1/3$ is achieved

steps: Laguerre-cell moments: the map moves at most like a cube root
Tilting one of three pieces swaps a thin slab: no better exponent
Squeezed from both sides, the exponent is exactly one third

before.label: Best known (Divol et al.)
before.note: constant depends on the atoms; Letrouit conjectured $1/2$

after.label: Claimed, 25 Sep 2026
after.note: uniform over all targets, and $1/3$ is sharp

achievement.note: For a uniform source on a convex body; the $W_1$ picture differs

voice.text: Three pieces sent to three atoms. Tilt the middle one and a thin slab swaps.
An upper bound and a tilting example meet at one third.
Claimed: one third, not one half.

sources.quote: Letrouit proved >1/3 fails for nonconvex sources and conjectured uniform square-root stability for uniform convex sources
the exponent 1/3 is sharp even for K=Y=[−1,1]^d and three-atom targets, disproving Letrouit's conjectured uniform 1/2 exponent
tilting the middle piece of a max of three affine functions keeps its mass but swaps a thin slab of source points between far-apart targets
W1 vs W2 distinction matters (a sharp W1^{1/4} estimate is consistent)
